The chapter on Russia will discuss its nuclear doctrine in greater detail, to include the multi-purpose utility of tactical weapons that are not counted as part of existing arms control regimes.
Both the United States and Russia are modernizing their nuclear arsenals, but only Russia is expanding their capabilities into multiple dual-use platforms with brand new warheads of various yields.

Mutually assured destruction is no longer enough to preserve stability in Europe, and even though the United States is modernizing its arsenal, the nuclear threat to Russia in terms of capability is unchanged.
